Unfamiliar

/un-fuh-MIL-yer/ · adjective

What It Means

Unfamiliar means not known or recognized, strange only because it has never been encountered before.

Stepping off the night train, Amara scanned the unfamiliar streets, unable to match a single building to the city she had pictured from her guidebook.

Worked Example

On his first morning at the new job, Theo stared at the warehouse's inventory software, an unfamiliar system full of menus he had never clicked and codes he had never read. By the end of the month, the very same screens felt like second nature.

The software was unfamiliar simply because Theo had never encountered it before, and once he gained experience with it, the strangeness disappeared entirely.

How Unfamiliar Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unknown

unknown: not known about at all

unrecognized

unrecognized: not identified from past experience

foreign

foreign: outside one's own experience or surroundings

Antonyms

familiar

familiar: well known from regular experience

recognizable

recognizable: easy to identify from past encounters

How Strong Is It? — new → unfamiliar → alien

new vs. unfamiliar

new vs. unfamiliar: Something new is simply recent, while something unfamiliar lies outside your experience entirely.

alien vs. unfamiliar

alien vs. unfamiliar: An unfamiliar place is one you have not encountered before, but an alien one feels so utterly foreign that nothing about it makes sense.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of unfamiliar.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — un-

Prefix — un-: not

Root — famili

Root — famili: from Latin familia, household

Suffix — -ar

Suffix — -ar: adjective ending, relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Unfamiliar stacks the prefix un-, 'not,' onto familiar, which comes from Latin familia, 'household.' Something familiar was originally something 'of the household,' known as well as your own family, so something unfamiliar is literally outside the household of your experience.

Use the root in a new word: familiarize

Use the root in a new word: familiarize: Before the road trip, Dev took an hour to familiarize himself with the rental car's controls, a verb grown from the same Latin root familia that hides inside unfamiliar.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Unfamiliar is about lack of prior exposure, not inherent oddness: a perfectly ordinary dish can be unfamiliar to someone who has never tried it. Note the prepositions: a person is unfamiliar with something, while something is unfamiliar to a person.
